1. NORTH INDIAN OCEAN AREA (MALAY PENINSULA WEST TO THE COAST OF 
AFRICA):
   A. TROPICAL CYCLONE SUMMARY: NONE.
   B. TROPICAL DISTURBANCE SUMMARY: NONE.
   C. SUBTROPICAL SYSTEM SUMMARY: NONE.
2. SOUTH INDIAN OCEAN AREA (135E WEST TO THE COAST OF AFRICA):
   A. TROPICAL CYCLONE SUMMARY: NONE.
   B. TROPICAL DISTURBANCE SUMMARY:
      (1) THE AREA OF CONVECTION (INVEST 97S) PREVIOUSLY LOCATED NEAR 
7.1S 68.9E IS NOW LOCATED NEAR 8.7S 68.6E, APPROXIMATELY 244 NM WEST-
SOUTHWEST OF DIEGO GARCIA. ANIMATED ENHANCED INFRARED (EIR) SATELLITE 
IMAGERY DEPICTS DEEP CONVECTION FLARING OVER A COMPACT LOW-LEVEL 
CIRCULATION CENTER (LLCC). A 251556Z ASCAT-B PASS SHOWS A DEFINED 
SURFACE CIRCULATION WITH 20-25 KT WINDS TO THE SOUTHWEST. 
ENVIRONMENTAL ANALYSIS REVEALS A MODERATELY FAVORABLE ENVIRONMENT FOR 
DEVELOPMENT WITH MODERATE VERTICAL WIND SHEAR (VWS) OF 15-20 KNOTS, 
MODERATE POLEWARD UPPER-LEVEL OUTFLOW, AND WARM SEA SURFACE 
TEMPERATURES (SST) OF 28-29 C. GLOBAL MODELS ARE IN GOOD AGREEMENT 
THAT INVEST 97S WILL CONTINUE TO SLOWLY CONSOLIDATE WHILE MAINTAINING 
A QUASI-STATIONARY MOTION OVER THE NEXT 24 HOURS.  MAXIMUM SUSTAINED 
SURFACE WINDS ARE ESTIMATED AT 23 TO 28 KNOTS. MINIMUM SEA LEVEL 
PRESSURE IS ESTIMATED TO BE NEAR 1008 MB. THE POTENTIAL FOR THE 
DEVELOPMENT OF A SIGNIFICANT TROPICAL CYCLONE WITHIN THE NEXT 24 HOURS 
IS MEDIUM.
      (2) THE AREA OF CONVECTION (INVEST 98S) PREVIOUSLY LOCATED NEAR 
8.9S 78.6E IS NOW LOCATED NEAR 11.0S 78.0E, APPROXIMATELY 395 NM 
SOUTHEAST OF DIEGO GARCIA. ANIMATED ENHANCED INFRARED (EIR) SATELLITE 
IMAGERY DEPICTS A PARTIALLY EXPOSED LOW-LEVEL CIRCULATION CENTER 
(LLCC), WITH RENEWED CONVECTIVE ACTIVITY NEAR THE CENTER.  A 250342Z 
ASCAT-C PASS REVEALED A DEFINED SURFACE CIRCULATION WITH NEAR GALE-
FORCE WINDS IN THE NORTHWEST QUADRANT. UPPER-LEVEL ANALYSIS INDICATES 
MODEST POLEWARD OUTFLOW ALOFT,  MODERATE (15-20 KTS) VERTICAL WIND 
SHEAR (VWS), AND WARM SEA SURFACE TEMPERATURES (SST) OF 28-29 C. 
GLOBAL MODELS DEPICT INCREASING VWS, WHICH WILL LIMIT FURTHER 
DEVELOPMENT AND BEGIN TO INDUCE WEAKENING OVER THE NEXT 24-48 HOURS AS 
THE SYSTEM MOVES GENERALLY POLEWARD. MAXIMUM SUSTAINED SURFACE WINDS 
ARE ESTIMATED AT 27 TO 32 KNOTS. MINIMUM SEA LEVEL PRESSURE IS 
ESTIMATED TO BE NEAR 1009 MB. THE POTENTIAL FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF A 
SIGNIFICANT TROPICAL CYCLONE WITHIN THE NEXT 24 HOURS IS LOW.
      (3) NO OTHER SUSPECT AREAS.
   C. SUBTROPICAL SYSTEM SUMMARY: NONE.//
